summary.text: Jeff Frese, a Republican small-business owner from Moraga, California, lost the November 3, 2026 election for California's 10th Congressional District to Mark DeSaulnier.
According to his Ballotpedia survey, he founded a snack company and sold it, now runs a skincare company, and earlier worked in product leadership at media companies.

paragraphs.text: Frese lives in Moraga, California. In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he describes himself as a husband, a father of three daughters, and a coach.
He earned a bachelor's degree in economics from the State University of New York, Cortland, according to the survey.
He says he worked in product leadership at CNN, Nickelodeon and MTV before entering business ownership.

Frese says he founded the snack company Fat Snax in his kitchen, grew it into a national brand with nationwide distribution, and sold it; he says he now runs a skincare company. His first job, he says, was at age eight selling wild plants door to door.
He was the Republican nominee for the 10th District in 2026, having advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary, and said the campaign took no special-interest money and had no consultants or staff.
His campaign focused on congressional term limits, affordability, and public safety.
He received 30.3% of the vote to Mark DeSaulnier's 69.7%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
